transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Laura Bennett (CISO, Silver Horizon), Mark Rivers (Head of Cloud Platforms), Priya Desai (Compliance Manager), Ethan Cole (Senior DevOps)

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through your data residency and compliance questions. I'm Ava, AE, with Daniel from our SE team. Laura? thanks for the time.
[00:10] Laura Bennett: Yeah thanks, Ava. Quick intro, I'm Laura, CISO at Silver Horizon. We're evaluating how to run some LLM features across retail banking funnels, but our primary constraint is where customer data can live and what logs can leave our environment.
[00:18] Daniel Cho: Totally understood. Can you walk us through the current architecture and the kinds of data we're most worried about?
[00:24] Mark Rivers: Sure. We run core services in Azure and GCP for redundancy. Most PII is kept in our private subnet, encrypted at rest with an HSM-backed KMS. We're exploring two product lines: one that handles basic support chat (low risk) and another that processes customer financial statements and health metrics (high risk, potentially subject to GLBA/HIPAA-like controls).
[00:39] Priya Desai: Our compliance ask is strict: any production customer-identifiable transcripts must remain in-country for EU customers, and for some high-risk workflows logs cannot be stored off-prem more than 7 days. We also need audit logs that show model version, prompt hashes, and who called the API.
[00:54] Ava Martinez: Thanks, that's clear. Redwood provides three deployment modes - Hosted, Dedicated, and Private - which give different tradeoffs. For strict residency and tight logging controls Private is usually the fit, but Dedicated with strict routing and region pinning can also work depending on log retention policies.
[01:10] Ethan Cole: When you say Private can be on-prem, is that a full air-gapped option? And how does KMS/HSM integration work?
[01:18] Daniel Cho: Private can be deployed into a customer's VPC or on-prem pack. For KMS we support customer-managed keys - you can bring your own key via KMS/HSM integrations; the Redwood control plane can be either customer-managed or we operate a thin control plane that never sees plaintext if configured that way. In air-gapped setups we run the inference runtime locally and logs can be kept entirely within customer infrastructure.
[01:40] Mark Rivers: Okay, so how do you handle telemetry and usage logs for Hosted? Because our legal team is worried about tokens and prompt contents being retained in Redwood systems.
[01:49] Ava Martinez: For Hosted we retain request/response logs for a short default window for troubleshooting and abuse detection, but we offer retention configuration and can disable request content logging for regulated customers; metadata and aggregated metrics can be kept without raw prompts. We also support field redaction and prompt hashing - so you can preserve observability while not storing raw PII.
[02:08] Priya Desai: What about GDPR requirements for EU subjects? If we have EU customers we need to keep their data inside EU and ensure processors have adequate protections.
[02:15] Daniel Cho: Redwood's Hosted deployment has region-specific endpoints, and we can ensure EU-only processing by using EU regions and contractual commitments. For deeper control, Private ensures the data never leaves your environment. We'll share our EU data processing addendum and SCCs if needed.
[02:30] Laura Bennett: Has Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II? And do you have ISO or HIPAA documentation?
[02:35] Ava Martinez: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; HIPAA attestation is available for customers with appropriate BAAs. I'll send the artifacts after this call.
[02:45] Mark Rivers: Can we get more detail on logging retention and the ability to remove logs on request - like an erase capability?
[02:52] Daniel Cho: In Dedicated and Private you control the retention entirely. For Hosted we have processes to delete data upon request for enterprise customers but if you need deterministic erase guarantees we recommend Private where logs are in your control. In Dedicated we can configure disk-level retention and restricted access; we also have playbooks for data deletion for Hosted enterprise plans.
[03:11] Ethan Cole: How do rollouts and model/versioning work in Private? We want the ops team to be able to pin a model and do canary tests without external toggles.
[03:19] Daniel Cho: The Private package comes with the same runtime and rollout tools; you can pin model versions, do canary and A/B and rollbacks. Telemetry hooks are local and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[03:29] Priya Desai: About audit logs: we need immutable logs for who invoked model, prompt hashes, model version, and any policy decisions. Is Redwood providing signed audit logs, or is that something we keep?
[03:39] Ava Martinez: We can provide both. In Hosted we provide audit logs and an export mechanism; for Dedicated/Private the logs are stored in your environment and you can forward to an immutable store. If you need signed logs we can integrate with HSM signing in Private deployments.
[03:52] Laura Bennett: A compliance question: certain workflows will include health data tied to customers - HIPAA is a big concern. What's the recommendation?
[03:58] Daniel Cho: HIPAA workflows should be on Private or Dedicated under a BAA. Hosted can be considered for non-PHI or if we have an explicit BAA and configuration to avoid retaining PHI. Best practice is Private for PHI where possible.
[04:12] Mark Rivers: Latency and cost tradeoffs are important. If we go Private on-prem, what's the expected performance difference compared to Hosted?
[04:19] Daniel Cho: If provisioned correctly, Private can match Dedicated/Hosted latency. The main differences are your hardware selection and network egress. Our runtime is optimized for GPUs and supports batching, KV cache - if you need low tail latency we'd size nodes accordingly. We normally run a short benchmark with sample traces to calibrate.
[04:37] Ava Martinez: Are there any hard deal-breakers from your side that would instantly push you away from Hosted?
[04:41] Laura Bennett: If prompts and transcripts for EU customers can leave the EU and be stored for more than 30 days by default that's a no-go. Also inability to integrate our HSM or to have deterministic log erasure would be tough.
[04:54] Ava Martinez: Understood. We can commit to EU-only processing for customer-scoped data and to bring your own key integrations in Dedicated/Private. We'll note the log erase playbook as a must-share.
[05:05] Priya Desai: One more question: how do you handle subcontractors/3rd-party processors and cross-border transfers? We need to list processors in our DPIA.
[05:14] Daniel Cho: We'll provide a list of subprocessors and our data processing addendum. For Private, subprocessors are minimized since you host the runtime. For Hosted we have standard subprocessors and we can offer contractual clauses to limit transfers.
[05:25] Mark Rivers: On the tech side: how are keys used for ephemeral caches? KV cache endpoints - do they ever write to an external store?
[05:32] Daniel Cho: KV cache is in-memory for the runtime and optionally backed to encrypted local storage. It does not cross regions unless you configure cross-region caching; by default it's local to the runtime instance.
[05:41] Ethan Cole: For the hosted API, do you support field-level redaction automatically or do we have to implement it client-side?
[05:48] Ava Martinez: We support both. We provide SDK helpers and server-side redaction rules for common PII. For stricter controls we recommend client-side or Private mode to avoid sending raw PII.
[05:58] Laura Bennett: For our procurement/legal process, we need to know lead times for Dedicated reserved capacity and Private deployments.
[06:04] Ava Martinez: Typical Dedicated reserved capacity starts with a 30-60 day lead time for GPU procurement and onboarding; Private timeline depends on on-prem readiness but small pilots are often completed in 2-4 weeks if we use your cloud VPC. On-prem air-gapped deployments have longer lead times. We'll map timing in the next email.
[06:20] Mark Rivers: Cost modeling: can you produce a sample TCO comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our estimated 10M tokens/mo usage with 20% of calls being high-risk work?
[06:29] Daniel Cho: Yes, we'll run a pricing model; we'll include expected GPU sizing, network egress costs, and infra ops.
[06:36] Priya Desai: Anything else on security certifications? We might need penetration test schedules and third-party attestations.
[06:42] Ava Martinez: We'll share pen test summary and frequency of audits; we can also do customer-led pen tests on Dedicated/Private under NDA.
[06:52] Laura Bennett: Great. To recap: we'll need SOC2/ISO/HIPAA docs, subprocessors list, EU DPA/SCCs, private deployment diagram, and a benchmark/pricing run. We'll review and get back with a procurement timeline next week.
[07:06] Ava Martinez: Yes, action items captured. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and set up the benchmark session.
[07:12] Mark Rivers: Thanks all.
[07:15] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "red- control plane" instead of "redwood control plane" in one spot), filler words, and some speaker overlap.
